opennyai_summary.3_May_2019__facts: The applicant has been convicted under the provisions of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act by JMFC, Badnawar, District Dhar and the order of conviction has been upheld by the learned appellate Court vide judgement dated 27.04.2019 passed in Criminal Appeal No.632/2010 wherein the applicant has been sentenced for six months R.I. with fine of Rs.1,000/- for committing adulteration and equivalent sentence for mis-branding the articles.
opennyai_summary.3_May_2019__decision:
After due consideration, the appeal is admitted for final hearing.
Learned counsel submits that considering this judgment, jail sentence be suspended.
The applicant has been found guilty by both the courts below, hence, it would be appropriate to call for the record.
As the applicant is in jail, record of the Courts below be requisitioned immediately so that the case may be listed in the next week.
opennyai_summary.arguments: Counsel for the applicant submits a citation of the apex Court in the case of Nemi Chand vs. State of Rajasthan (2016) 2 AICLR 479 in which it has been held that in a case when the appellant convicted under the provisions of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, he may be dealt with as per the provisions of Food, Safety and Adulteration Act, 2006 and be subjected to only penalty of depositing a sum of money instead of jail term.
opennyai_summary.final__PREAMBLE:

3
 High Court Of Madhya Pradesh, Bench At Indore
 Criminal Revision No.2226 Of 2019
 (Ashok Vs State Of Madhya Pradesh)
Indore, Dated 13.05.2019
opennyai_summary.final__facts:
The applicant was earlier convicted under the provisions of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (for short the Act of 1954) by JMFC Badnawr vide judgment dated 26.10.2017 passed in Criminal Case No.632/2010 and sentenced to six-six months RI with fine of Rs.1000/- -1000/- for committing offences under Section 16(A)(A-1) of the Act of 1954 for misbranding and adulteration.
The provisions under which the conviction has been affirmed are Section 7(2) read with Section 16(A)(A-1) of the Act of 1954.
In the Apex Court judgment, the accused-Nemi Chand/appellant was convicted under Section 7/16 of the Act of 1954 for committing offence of misbranding and was HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH, BENCH AT INDORE CRIMINAL REVISION NO.2226 OF 2019 (ASHOK VS STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH) sentenced to undergo six months RI with fine of Rs.1000/- with default imprisonment sentence.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Considered.
In view of the citation of Apex Court which squarely covers the present case, it would be in propriety to substitute the sentence of imprisonment and fine with penalty of Rs.50,000/- in respect of offence for misbranding and further Rs.50,000/- in respect of offence for adulteration.
opennyai_summary.final__decision:
Thus, in all,
Rs.1.00 lac be imposed on the applicant in respect of both the offences.
The applicant shall deposit this amount before the trial Court within a period of two months.
On depositing such amount, his bail bonds shall be discharged.
Presently, his jail sentence is being suspended so that he can acquire the desired fund of Rs.1.00 lac.
The substantive jail sentence is HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH, BENCH AT INDORE CRIMINAL REVISION NO.2226 OF 2019 (ASHOK VS STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH) suspended on furnishing Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand) by the applicant with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his regular appearance before the trial Court on 22/07/2019 and on all other dates given by the trial Court.
Thus it is specifically directed that copy of this order be sent to trial Court with a direction that if the applicant does not deposit Rs.1.00 lac within a period of two months from today, then the order of appellate Court shall be revived and he shall suffer the jail sentence as already imposed by the appellate Court.
On deposition of Rs.1.00 lac by the applicant, the jail sentence and fine amount as prescribed in the impugned order shall stand quashed and returned to applicant.
This criminal revision is disposed of with conviction having been maintained but partly allowed in terms of sentence.
At this point of time, learned counsel for the applicant submits that he undertakes to deposit penalty of Rs.1.00 lac by 14th May 2019.
In that event, the applicant be released forthwith by the learned trial Court on deposition of penalty of Rs.1.00 lac.
